currentWork.title: FINAL.28 routing asset cache fix — production released and verified
currentWork.releaseStatus: FINAL.28 is live. PR #154 merged to main at 676e2e12debe529f620895b3c5911d855ef14768. Vercel production dpl_F1zukXiJkKwxfKDgwjUBRqzusFAy is READY. GitHub Pages run 37495335651 succeeded, main push browser regression run 37495337396 passed, and the live version endpoint reports 2026.10.07-FINAL.28.
rootCause: The app HTML version advanced through FINAL.27, but the external routing script URL remained fixed at truck-routing.js?v=2026.10.06-TRUCK-ROUTE.

A client could therefore load FINAL.27 HTML while reusing an older cached routing module. FINAL.27's route draw code expected section.highlight, while older routeSections output did not provide highlight. In that mixed-version state, every route span evaluates as non-priority and renders blue.
This is a client asset-version/cache compatibility defect, independent of the already-verified ORS waycategory Highway/Tollways bit semantics.
scope: truck-routing.js is now requested with ?v=2026.10.07-FINAL.28, matching the application release.
Real Edge validation asserts version.json, HTML routing-script query and runtime routing assetVersion agree.
Route drawing has backward compatibility: a span is red when section.highlight, section.motorway or section.tollway is true, so legacy section objects do not turn known priority spans blue.
Highway/toll spans remain red (#dc2626), ordinary spans remain blue (#2563eb), and the FINAL.27 fullscreen PIN/detail fix remains unchanged.
Analytics engine, DB/schema, tasks, orders, visits, HGV profile and user data remain unchanged.
